_comment: Ship-neutral-first: every map carries IDENTITY grade values ([1,1,1], vignette 0) by default so atmosphere.gd is live end-to-end with no visible change on its own; specific maps below tune inn/street/floodplains/cave_mouth/etc for real -- see CLAUDE.md's rollout blocks. `meta.phase_thresholds` is LIVE: game.gd's `_build_sim` reads this dict and passes {dusk_at, night_at} into WIGame's `phase_config` ctor arg -- if that wiring is ever removed, WIGame._phase_config silently falls back to its own hardcoded 40/90 defaults (see wi_game.gd's phase() doc comment), so this dict genuinely drives phase timing, not just documentation. Current values (100/225, tuned for a 'dark before you reach Liscor' pacing target) size the honest inn->Liscor onboarding route (measured N~60 post-Warrior-sleep actions to arrive at street; gate_district_walkthrough hits actions_since_sleep==62 at map_changed{street}) to land in LATE DAY with dusk ~38 actions later (dusk_at 100 ~=1.6xN; night_at 225 = 2.25x dusk_at). TRAP: changing dusk/night here genuinely moves phase_changed in every event stream -- same full-canonical-seed-reverify rule as combat data (CLAUDE.md's Equipment block). atmosphere_check.json's dusk-crossing route is SIZED to dusk_at and must stay in lockstep with it. `meta.light_energy_by_phase` is read by atmosphere.gd's `light_multiplier` (day 0.0 keeps every light invisible by day, preserving the daylight look).

sewers._comment: A DARK, time-invariant pin (cave_mouth precedent values) -- the sewers read the same at any phase. Phosphor/shaft lights glow only at dusk/night (light_energy_by_phase day=0.0); the always-on pond_glints/dust ambience carries the day-phase atmosphere against this grade.

guild._comment: The Adventurer's Guild interior -- "warm bureaucratic". Warmer/ambery than the inn's own grade (lamp-and-parchment read for a paperwork hall), less vignette than the street (a busy, populated room, not an oppressive one).

inn_upstairs._comment: The inn's second floor -- "warm dim". TIME-INVARIANT (same sewers/deep_tunnels precedent for a room that doesn't see the outside clock directly) rather than day/dusk/night-graded like the guild's windowed hall: a small private upstairs room reads the same at 2pm or midnight. Reuses the inn's OWN dusk grade verbatim ([0.85,0.72,0.55]) as the permanent pin -- literally 'always looks like the warm end of the day downstairs', a direct, defensible reuse rather than inventing a new palette. Same vignette as the inn (0.4) -- enclosed but not oppressive, matching a lived-in room rather than a dungeon.

barracks._comment: The Watch barracks -- "stern"/cool institutional ('barracks = stern'). Cool blue-grey, desaturated against the guild's warm amber (0.3 vignette) and the street's night-dark blue (0.44) -- reads as a spare, dutiful room rather than a welcoming or oppressive one. TIME-INVARIANT (inn_upstairs/sewers precedent): a barracks is staffed day and night, so it reads the same at any phase rather than tracking the outside clock.

runners_guild._comment: The Runner's Guild -- "brisk practical". Neutral-warm parchment/ledger tone, brighter and less saturated than the Guild's own amber (guild's [1.0,0.94,0.82]) and warmer than the barracks' cool blue-grey ([0.68,0.74,0.82]) -- a working counter-and-ledgers room, busy rather than bureaucratic or stern. TIME-INVARIANT (barracks/inn_upstairs/sewers precedent): couriers keep counter hours day and night (deliveries complete within any waking), so the room reads the same at any phase.

ruin_surface._comment: The ruin card -- "cold daylight, dusty". A SURFACE ruin sees real weather (unlike sewers/deep_tunnels' time-invariant underground pins), so it is day/dusk/night graded like inn/street/floodplains, just cooler and flatter than any of their [1,1,1]-identity day grades -- an overcast, slightly desaturated read rather than the warm/bright outdoor look. Vignette between floodplains (0.4) and sewers (0.45) -- exposed but ruined, not oppressive. The 'dusty' half of the brief is a texture/ambience call (floor tile choice + a future dust-mote emitter), not a color-grade one -- left to a later art/ambience task, ship-neutral here.

garden._comment: The only card in the game that is BOTH identity-at-every-phase AND vignette 0.0 -- every other time-invariant pin above (sewers/inn_upstairs/barracks/runners_guild) holds a DARK/desaturated triple constant across phases; this is the same mechanism (atmosphere.gd's apply() is a pure per-(map,phase) lookup, oblivious to whether the three arrays happen to be equal -- traced, not assumed, before landing this one-liner) applied to the IDENTITY grade instead. The eyes-closed test IS the mood system itself: if the screen never dims and never vignettes on this map, you are in the garden. No `arena_moods` entry, ever -- combat can never start here (the sim guard in wi_game.gd's start_combat), so an arena card would itself be a bug.

deep_tunnels._comment: The Raskghar descent -- the DARKEST pin in the game, time-invariant (below the sewers, no daylight ever reaches it). Meaningfully darker + colder than the sewers' [0.3,0.32,0.45] so the descent visibly escalates; a stronger vignette (0.55) squeezes the readable space to a lantern's reach. Any prop lights glow at every phase intent (light_energy day=0.0 still keeps day flat, so the tunnels lean on their own cold ambience).

riverfarm_village._comment: 8b R1 (issue #10). "harvest light" -- the ONLY map whose day grade tips warm (identity everywhere else is [1,1,1]); deep-blue night per spec sec.1. Values per docs/design/riverfarm-art/direction.md's Mood-card DRAFT, windowed-verified at day+dusk this task (the contrast IS the storytelling, art handoff).

witch_hollow._comment: 8b R1 (issue #10). "green shade" -- never reaches identity white even at day (canopy); dusk is the map's home key (firefly-dense per spec); vignette 0.50 > sewers' 0.45 (enclosure without an underground pin). Values per direction.md's Mood-card DRAFT.

sewers_nest._comment: Sewers combat inherits the same dark cave pin as the map (cave_mouth values), so the vermin/nest fights read as underground.

deep_warren._comment: The boss arena inherits the deep_tunnels darkest pin so the Awakened Raskghar fight reads as the lowest, coldest point of the descent (matches the map grade the player crosses to reach it).
